title: Console + Rollouts integration sync (error budgets in canary + UI)
summary: PMs and engineering aligned on how error budget status will flow from SLO calculations into canary analysis and Console UI. The group agreed on a minimal contract for a budget-check endpoint (tier/service/scope, status + remaining, burn-rate, and “effective mode” warn/soft-block/hard-block), how canary will label risk, and what the UI should show when a rollout is blocked. Open items include scope rules (per-route vs per-model) and how Dedicated customer-specific budgets are permissioned in Console.
topics: Budget-check API contract for canary + deploy gates
How canary analyzer consumes budget status and labels results
Console UX for ‘blocked due to error budget’ and override flow
Dedicated permissions and avoiding data leakage
questions: Do we block on “budget exhausted” only, or also on fast burn (e.g., 2h burn > threshold) for soft-block?
What is the MVP scope key: service+tier, or route+tier, or model+tier?
Where do overrides live (control plane vs rollout service) and how does Console display audit/TTL?
action_items: Benji Okafor - Draft a v1 JSON response for /reliability/budget-check with fields needed by canary + Console (status, remaining, burn rates, mode) - Due 2026-02-25
Aisha Bello - Confirm burn-rate windows we will expose to UI (e.g., 1h/6h/3d) and naming conventions - Due 2026-02-26
Jada Williams - Add a canary analyzer mapping from budget-check response to ‘Budget risk’ labels (green/yellow/red) + gating decision stub - Due 2026-02-27
Kenji Nakamura - Update Rollout screen UX copy and states: warning banner vs blocked modal vs override affordance - Due 2026-02-27
Chloe Martin - Decide MVP scope key for budgets shown in Console (service-tier minimum) and capture in Console spec - Due 2026-02-28
Jordan Lee - Confirm how tier is derived for requests and how Dedicated customer_id scoping is represented without leaking - Due 2026-02-28
Sergio Costa - Provide the canonical dashboard link template (tier/region/model/route filters) that Console can deep-link to - Due 2026-02-28
next_steps: Benji to circulate endpoint contract proposal in #eng-platform with example payloads for Hosted and Dedicated.
Chloe/Kenji to post updated UI wire notes (blocked + warning states) and request async review from SRE + Control Plane.
Jada to wire a mock budget-check call in staging canary flow behind a feature flag; no blocking yet.
Follow-up sync in one week to finalize MVP scope key and override audit display.
transcript:
Meeting: Console + Rollouts integration sync (error budgets in canary + UI)
Recorded: Feb 20, 2026 17:00 UTC
Duration: 46 min
Attendees (Redwood): Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes, Chloe Martin, Jada Williams, Kenji Nakamura, Aisha Bello, Benji Okafor, Jordan Lee, Sergio Costa, Ethan Park

---

[00:00] Marissa Cole: Okay, cool. Let’s get started. This is the Console and Rollouts integration sync for error budgets. Goal today is to get alignment on, one, what canary needs to read to label a rollout as “at risk”, and two, how Console shows that without becoming like… a second SRE tool.

[00:18] Chloe Martin: Yeah, and also, what’s the absolute minimum contract from the budget service. Like, we can build UI around it, but we need stable fields.

[00:27] Ethan Park: Makes sense. Benji and I can talk about what the control plane endpoint can return. We’ve got the first pass in the PR, but it’s very “warn-only” right now.

[00:37] Paula Mendes: And from Rollouts PM side, we need the gating semantics spelled out: warn-only, soft-block, hard-block. And what triggers which.

[00:47] Aisha Bello: Plus, the SRE ask is that whatever you show in Console aligns with the SLO definitions. We don’t want “budget remaining 80%” in UI but a different calculation in alerts.

[00:57] Marissa Cole: Yep. Okay. Jada, can you summarize what canary analyzer is doing today?

[01:03] Jada Williams: Sure. Canary today runs a set of checks: error rate, latency deltas, some route-level counters. It produces a pass/warn/fail and it can halt progressive rollout. But it only uses live metrics for the canary window.

[01:19] Jada Williams: What we want is: pull “budget status” at time of analysis, so if the service is already burning budget, you don’t keep pushing more changes. Or at least you get a very loud warning.

[01:32] Kenji Nakamura: UX-wise, we need something that’s explainable. “Blocked because error budget is exhausted” is fine. “Blocked because burn rate above 2.3” is not fine.

[01:43] Sergio Costa: And when you click through, you should land on the SLO dashboard panel that shows the burn. Otherwise people argue with the UI.

[01:50] Marissa Cole: Great. Benji, can you talk what the endpoint is currently returning and what we can add?

[01:56] Benji Okafor: Right now it’s basically a boolean-ish response: budget_ok true/false based on remaining in a rolling 30d window. That was enough for the deploy gate stub.

[02:10] Benji Okafor: For canary + Console, I think we need richer fields: budget_remaining_percent, budget_remaining_minutes maybe, and burn rates. But we have to be careful to not expose like a million labels.

[02:25] Jordan Lee: Also, scope. Because if the policy engine is calling this, it will pass tier and service. But you might want route or model. That changes cardinality.

[02:36] Aisha Bello: The SRE preference is: start with service+tier. The SLOs are defined per journey, but the enforcement should be on a bounded set of services at first.

[02:47] Chloe Martin: For Console, we can still display filters, but if budget is computed only at service-tier we just say that. Like “Budget scope: gateway (Hosted)”.

[03:01] Marissa Cole: Okay, so service+tier for MVP. What about region?

[03:06] Sergio Costa: Dashboards will definitely break down by region, but I’m okay if the gating is global per tier initially. Region-level gating can come later.

[03:15] Ethan Park: Yeah, gating by region is complicated because deploys are region staged. We’d need to pass “rollout region” into the check.

[03:23] Paula Mendes: Let’s not block that. For MVP, if budget is bad globally, block. If budget is good globally, proceed, and canary still watches region metrics.

[03:33] Kenji Nakamura: That’s also easier to explain.

[03:37] Marissa Cole: Great. So: service+tier, global. Now: what are the states we want?

[03:44] Aisha Bello: SRE terms: “healthy”, “at risk”, “exhausted”. At risk could be “fast burn” even if remaining is non-zero.

[03:54] Jada Williams: That would be super helpful. Because you can have 60% remaining but you’re burning at, like, 10x in the last hour.

[04:02] Benji Okafor: We can return an enum. Something like status: OK | AT_RISK | EXHAUSTED. And then mode: WARN | SOFT_BLOCK | HARD_BLOCK.

[04:12] Chloe Martin: Wait, what’s the difference between status and mode?

[04:15] Benji Okafor: Status is computed from budgets and burn. Mode is policy-driven. Like, the same status could be warn-only for some services during pilot.

[04:25] Jordan Lee: Exactly. Policy engine decides effective enforcement. We can calculate status and then the policy decides what to do with it.

[04:33] Marissa Cole: That’s good. UI can show status as the truth, and show whether the rollout is blocked because policy says block.

[04:41] Kenji Nakamura: Yep. Then we can show “This org is in warn-only for error budgets” or “This service is in soft-block”.

[04:50] Paula Mendes: I want to be careful: we don’t want org-level. It’s per service and tier, at least.

[04:55] Jordan Lee: Right. It’d be a policy mapping on (service, tier). Potentially also environment.

[05:02] Sergio Costa: Also, the dashboard deep link should include tier. We’ve had issues where people open the dashboard and they’re looking at Dedicated by accident.

[05:10] Chloe Martin: Okay, we can do that. The UI should always display the selected tier.

[05:16] Marissa Cole: Let’s talk fields. Aisha, what burn windows are we standardizing?

[05:21] Aisha Bello: The org standard doc says multi-window, typically 1h and 6h fast burn, plus something like 3d for slow burn. For UI, I’d expose at least the fast window pair.

[05:34] Aisha Bello: But please don’t label it “1h burn” without context. We can say “Fast burn detected (last 1h/6h)”.

[05:43] Kenji Nakamura: Okay, for UX we can have a “Why?” link. Clicking it shows the two windows and a link to the burn chart.

[05:52] Jada Williams: For canary analyzer, we can treat AT_RISK as adding a warning label, and EXHAUSTED as failing the gate if mode is blocking.

[06:03] Ethan Park: And the deploy gate will use the same endpoint. That’s important, one source.

[06:09] Marissa Cole: Yes. We should not have separate endpoints.

[06:12] Benji Okafor: Okay. Proposed response fields, rough:
- scope: service, tier
- status: OK/AT_RISK/EXHAUSTED
- remaining: percent
- burn_rates: 1h, 6h, 3d maybe
- effective_mode: WARN_ONLY / SOFT_BLOCK / HARD_BLOCK
- dashboard_url
- as_of timestamp

[06:35] Chloe Martin: That’s enough for UI.

[06:36] Sergio Costa: Please include dashboard_url as a template or a direct link. If we try to build it client-side, it will drift.

[06:44] Jordan Lee: dashboard_url can come from config. The budget service can embed it.

[06:49] Paula Mendes: What about overrides? We need that story.

[06:53] Ethan Park: Today overrides are a token you can pass to the deploy gate to bypass. It gets logged in control plane.

[07:02] Benji Okafor: The question is: should canary support override too, or only deploy.

[07:07] Jada Williams: It should, because otherwise people will override deploy and then canary blocks and they’re confused.

[07:14] Kenji Nakamura: UX needs a consistent affordance. If blocked, you can “Request override” or “Override with token”. Something like that.

[07:23] Marissa Cole: We can do “override with token” for internal users first. Request flow later.

[07:28] Paula Mendes: Agree. MVP: show blocked state, show where to go to get override.

[07:34] Aisha Bello: And SRE requirement: every override needs TTL and reason. Otherwise we just bypass budgets permanently.

[07:42] Jordan Lee: That’s policy engine territory. We can store override records with expiry and reason in control plane.

[07:50] Chloe Martin: How does Console show that? Like, if a rollout is blocked but an override exists?

[07:56] Kenji Nakamura: It should show a banner: “Override active until X, created by Y” and link to audit.

[08:02] Sergio Costa: And ideally also show the budget status still. Because override doesn’t mean budget is okay.

[08:08] Marissa Cole: Yes, override is an exception, not a resolution.

[08:13] Jada Williams: Implementation detail: canary needs to know if an override token was used, to tag the analysis result.

[08:20] Benji Okafor: We can include in the response a field “override_applied”: true/false if token is presented. Or canary can just log it.

[08:28] Jordan Lee: Better to keep that local. The endpoint can return “override_required”: true maybe? Hmm.

[08:34] Ethan Park: The endpoint can just evaluate with or without override. If override token present, it returns effective_mode WARN, basically.

[08:44] Paula Mendes: That’s confusing. I’d rather it returns “mode would be HARD_BLOCK, but override applied.”

[08:51] Kenji Nakamura: Yeah, we need “You are proceeding under override.”

[08:55] Benji Okafor: Okay. Field: enforcement_decision: ALLOW | WARN | BLOCK, and separate: policy_mode and override_applied. Something like that.

[09:10] Chloe Martin: Let’s not overcomplicate, but yes we need to show override applied.

[09:15] Marissa Cole: We’ll capture it. Benji, can you propose the exact response and send after.

[09:21] Benji Okafor: Yep.

[09:23] Marissa Cole: Next topic: Dedicated. We have to be careful because budgets can be customer-specific. Jordan, what’s the plan there?

[09:31] Jordan Lee: So Dedicated tier: budgets can be calculated per pool and per customer, but we can’t expose that broadly. For MVP, I suggest budgets computed at the service-tier level for Dedicated control plane components, not per customer.

[09:45] Aisha Bello: SRE agrees. Customer-level SLOs are more sensitive and also harder to compute correctly. We’ll add that later with permissioning.

[09:54] Chloe Martin: For Console, does that mean Dedicated customers don’t see an “error budget” view?

[09:58] Marissa Cole: The MVP we’re building is internal Console first, right?

[10:02] Chloe Martin: Mixed. There is an internal view and a customer-facing view request on the roadmap. But MVP should not leak.

[10:09] Sergio Costa: If customer-facing, we need a separate dataset and strict filters. Otherwise, someone can switch customer_id in the UI.

[10:16] Kenji Nakamura: UX can also help by not presenting fields that imply you can switch customers.

[10:22] Paula Mendes: Also, a Dedicated customer might be rolling out a config or a model version. They might see a block and they’ll ask “why are you blocking me?”

[10:31] Aisha Bello: Exactly. That’s a future problem. For now, we keep the gating internal, for Redwood deploys.

[10:38] Marissa Cole: Okay, so for this meeting: we’re wiring budgets into rollout tooling used by Redwood engineers. Not end-customer self-serve.

[10:47] Chloe Martin: Cool. Then we can keep permissions simpler.

[10:50] Marissa Cole: Back to UI. Kenji, what’s the proposal for showing budget in canary screen?

[10:56] Kenji Nakamura: I’ve got three states:
1) No budget data: show “Budget status unavailable” gray info, don’t block.
2) Budget warning: yellow banner “Error budget at risk (fast burn)”, link to dashboard.
3) Blocked: red modal or banner “Rollout blocked: error budget exhausted”, with two CTAs: “View dashboards” and “Override (token)”.

[11:22] Kenji Nakamura: Also, a small pill next to canary result: “Budget: OK/At risk/Exhausted”.

[11:30] Jada Williams: That’s good. Canary analyzer can attach that pill value from the endpoint.

[11:35] Paula Mendes: We should also show the as-of time. Otherwise it’s like “was this computed yesterday?”

[11:41] Chloe Martin: Yes, timestamp.

[11:43] Benji Okafor: We can include as_of and maybe staleness seconds.

[11:47] Sergio Costa: If staleness > 10 minutes, I would treat as unknown. Metrics pipeline can lag.

[11:54] Aisha Bello: We should be explicit: if data is stale, do not block. Warn only.

[12:01] Jordan Lee: That’s a policy decision, but yes.

[12:04] Ethan Park: We can implement default behavior: missing/stale => allow with warning.

[12:11] Marissa Cole: That seems right for pilot.

[12:15] Marissa Cole: Now, integration points. Jada, where does canary run? Can it call control plane?

[12:21] Jada Williams: Canary runs in our perf-canary service, it can call internal APIs. We’ll need auth and a stable endpoint.

[12:29] Ethan Park: Control plane can expose an internal endpoint behind service auth. That’s fine.

[12:36] Chloe Martin: Is control plane the right owner though? Or should it be slo-toolkit service?

[12:41] Aisha Bello: For compute, it’s a scheduled job and storage. But for “checking” at deploy time, control plane is fine because it’s already in the path.

[12:52] Jordan Lee: Also the policy evaluation hook is in control plane, so it can apply effective_mode.

[12:58] Marissa Cole: Great. Console needs to fetch budget status too, for the canary detail view. Should Console call control plane, or should it call rollout service?

[13:09] Chloe Martin: I’d prefer it reads from rollout service because that keeps Console decoupled from control plane availability. But the source of truth is control plane.

[13:20] Jada Williams: The canary result can store the budget snapshot it used. Then Console just renders the snapshot. That prevents drift and reduces calls.

[13:28] Kenji Nakamura: That’s ideal for UX. It also avoids “it changed while you were looking.”

[13:33] Sergio Costa: But you still want a “current budget” view somewhere.

[13:36] Chloe Martin: Separate page. For canary detail, snapshot.

[13:40] Marissa Cole: Okay. So for canary screen: snapshot stored with canary analysis. For a general “Budget” page in Console: we can call the budget service live later.

[13:54] Paula Mendes: And for gating, rollout service should call live at each stage transition.

[14:00] Jordan Lee: Careful. If rollout is stage-based, you may want to check budget at each progression, yes.

[14:06] Ethan Park: That’s in PR 18511 direction, but we’re not there yet. For now, canary only.

[14:14] Marissa Cole: Correct. This is MVP: canary labels + UI. Next milestone adds actual blocking.

[14:23] Aisha Bello: Just make sure that when you do blocking, it is scoped. You don’t want to block all deploys because one model’s embeddings route is burning.

[14:33] Chloe Martin: That brings us back to scope key. We said service-tier for MVP. But long-term, we probably do per journey.

[14:42] Sergio Costa: Yeah, journey-based SLOs are “chat streaming”, “embeddings”, etc. If we only have service-tier, we might block changes unrelated to the burning journey.

[14:51] Jada Williams: That’s true, but from tooling perspective, one key is simpler. And it’s pilot.

[14:57] Paula Mendes: For rollouts, false positives are killer. We should keep it broad initially but only for selected services.

[15:06] Aisha Bello: Exactly. Pilot services: gateway, routing, control plane. That’s it.

[15:12] Ethan Park: And runtime maybe later.

[15:15] Marissa Cole: Okay. Console should show “Scope: gateway Hosted” so engineers understand it’s broad.

[15:23] Kenji Nakamura: We can add a small line: “This gate is evaluated at the service level (not per route/model).”

[15:31] Chloe Martin: Great.

[15:34] Marissa Cole: Let’s talk copy. Kenji, can you propose consistent strings? Especially “error budget” vs “reliability budget”.

[15:41] Kenji Nakamura: I’d stick with “Error budget” because that’s what SRE uses. But we can add tooltip: “Error budget measures allowed failures vs SLO.”

[15:50] Aisha Bello: Please do not rename it. We’ve had debates and “reliability budget” confuses people.

[15:56] Marissa Cole: Fine.

[15:58] Sergio Costa: Also, we should avoid showing the raw number of errors. It’s not helpful and might cause confusion.

[16:05] Chloe Martin: Show remaining percent and maybe “days left at current burn” later.

[16:10] Paula Mendes: Forecasting is a future enhancement. MVP just status.

[16:16] Jada Williams: One more: what happens if endpoint is down? Can we degrade gracefully?

[16:22] Ethan Park: If control plane endpoint is down, canary should treat as unknown. No blocking. But log an internal warning.

[16:30] Aisha Bello: And we should alert on that. If budget-check is down, we lose enforcement.

[16:36] Benji Okafor: We can add SLO to the budget-check endpoint too. (laugh)

[16:40] Marissa Cole: Don’t.

[16:41] (crosstalk)

[16:45] Marissa Cole: Okay, last chunk: rollout gating path. Paula, what do you need for the PRD update?

[16:52] Paula Mendes: I need a crisp statement: canary will call budget-check, store a snapshot, show it in UI. Gating remains warn-only in this phase. Next phase, rollout progression can consult budget status and block when exhausted.

[17:09] Paula Mendes: Also I need which fields are required for UI. Kenji’s states, plus link to dashboards.

[17:16] Marissa Cole: Chloe, you’ll update Console spec with this?

[17:19] Chloe Martin: Yes. I’ll write the section “Error budget integration (MVP)” and include the payload fields and UX states.

[17:28] Kenji Nakamura: I’ll update wire notes.

[17:30] Marissa Cole: Great. Aisha, anything else from SRE?

[17:34] Aisha Bello: Two things:
One, use the canonical tier label, do not invent “enterprise” or “pro”. It’s Hosted vs Dedicated.
Two, show exclusions somewhere? Maybe not in the UI, but at least link to the SLO definition page.

[17:50] Chloe Martin: We can include a “What counts?” link that goes to the internal Confluence page.

[17:55] Kenji Nakamura: That’s helpful.

[17:57] Sergio Costa: If you do that, please make sure it’s the stable URL, not someone’s draft.

[18:03] Marissa Cole: Noted.

[18:06] Jordan Lee: Also, policy engine needs to know the tier for a rollout context. For Hosted it’s straightforward. For Dedicated, if you’re deploying a service used by both tiers, what tier do you check?

[18:18] Ethan Park: Good question. For shared services, we might need to evaluate both budgets. But for MVP we’re scoping it to tier-specific services.

[18:28] Aisha Bello: Yeah, we can avoid shared services in pilot.

[18:31] Paula Mendes: But long term we’ll need multi-scope checks.

[18:36] Marissa Cole: Capture as open question. We’re not solving today.

[18:41] Chloe Martin: Yep.

[18:43] Marissa Cole: Alright, let’s do a quick recap and assign owners.

[18:48] Marissa Cole: Benji: draft the v1 endpoint response with fields: status, remaining, burn rates, effective mode, dashboard URL, timestamps, plus override applied indicator.

[18:59] Benji Okafor: Yep.

[19:00] Marissa Cole: Aisha: confirm which burn windows we expose and naming.

[19:04] Aisha Bello: Yep.

[19:06] Marissa Cole: Jada: canary analyzer integration, label mapping, store snapshot.

[19:12] Jada Williams: Yes.

[19:13] Marissa Cole: Kenji: update UX copy and blocked/warn states.

[19:18] Kenji Nakamura: Yep.

[19:19] Marissa Cole: Chloe: update Console spec, document scope key and deep links.

[19:24] Chloe Martin: Will do.

[19:26] Marissa Cole: Sergio: provide the canonical dashboard links and any required query params.

[19:32] Sergio Costa: Yep, I’ll send a template.

[19:35] Marissa Cole: Jordan: confirm tier derivation and how we avoid Dedicated customer leakage in the future version.

[19:42] Jordan Lee: Yep.

[19:44] Marissa Cole: Great. Anything else?

[19:47] Ethan Park: Just one: can we keep the endpoint naming consistent with other control plane APIs. I’ll review the path once Benji sends the payload.

[19:54] Marissa Cole: Cool.

[19:55] Paula Mendes: And I’ll update the PRD with the MVP statement.

[20:00] Marissa Cole: Awesome. Thanks everyone.

---

(End of transcript. Note: Fireflies transcription contained minor crosstalk and possible acronym errors.)
